proposals.before: In Zu Yi’s time there was Wu Xian;
proposals.after: In Zu Yi’s time there was Wu Hsien;
proposals.reason: Chinese 巫賢 is a different person from 巫咸 (Wu Xian) in the previous sentence; English wrongly uses the same spelling for both.

proposals.before: In Zu Yi's time, there was Wu Xian;
proposals.after: In Zu Yi's time, there was Wu Hsien;
proposals.reason: Chinese 巫賢 is a different person from 巫咸 (Wu Xian) in the previous sentence; English wrongly uses the same spelling for both.

proposals.before: The Yan ruler escorted Duke Huan of Qi out of the border. Duke Huan then ceded to Yan the territory he had taken, making Yan jointly pay tribute to the Son of Heaven, as in the duty during the time of Chengzhou;
proposals.after: The Yan ruler escorted Duke Huan of Qi out of the border. Duke Huan then ceded to Yan the territory to which Yan had come, making Yan jointly pay tribute to the Son of Heaven, as in the duty during the time of Chengzhou;
proposals.reason: Chinese 燕所至地 means the lands as far as Yan (the escort) had reached, not territory Duke Huan 'had taken'.

proposals.before: General Shi Bei and the common people counterattacked the heir apparent Ping. He was killed, and his body was displayed as a warning.
proposals.after: General Shi Bei and the common people counterattacked the heir apparent Ping. General Shi Bei died and was displayed as a warning.
proposals.reason: Chinese 將軍市被死，以徇 makes Shi Bei the one who died and was displayed; idiomatic 'He was killed' wrongly suggests Ping.

proposals.before: King Yi succeeded for twelve years and died. His son Yan Kuai succeeded.
proposals.after: King Yi reigned for twelve years and died. His son Yan Kuai succeeded.
proposals.reason: 立十二年 means he was on the throne twelve years; 'succeeded for twelve years' mistranslates the reign length.

proposals.before: Guo Kui said: "If the king must wish to attract scholars, start with Kui first.
proposals.after: Guo Kui said: "If the king truly wishes to attract scholars, start with Kui first.
proposals.reason: 必欲 means the king truly/certainly wishes to attract scholars; 'must wish' wrongly implies obligation.

proposals.before: Yan saw that Zhao had been repeatedly hard-pressed by Qin, and that Lian Po had left, so they made Pang Nuan the general. They wished to take advantage of Zhao's weakness to attack it.
proposals.after: Yan saw that Zhao had been repeatedly hard-pressed by Qin, that Lian Po had left, and that Pang Nuan had been made general. They wished to take advantage of Zhao's weakness to attack it.
proposals.reason: In 令龐煖將也 Yan observes that Zhao made Pang Nuan general; idiomatic 'they made' wrongly makes Yan the appointer.

proposals.before: Yan saw that Zhao had been repeatedly hard pressed by Qin, and Lian Po had left, so they made Pang Nuan general. They wished to take advantage of Zhao's weakness to attack it.
proposals.after: Yan saw that Zhao had been repeatedly hard pressed by Qin, and Lian Po had left, and that Pang Nuan had been made general. They wished to take advantage of Zhao's weakness to attack it.
proposals.reason: Same referent error: 令龐煖將也 is Zhao appointing Pang Nuan, not Yan.

decisions.after: In Zu Yi’s time there was another Wu Xian, the preceding minister's son;
decisions.reason: 巫咸 and his son 巫賢 are distinct Shang ministers but have the same standard pinyin, Wū Xián. Calling only the son 'Wu Hsien' would mix romanization systems; identifying the family relationship disambiguates him without inventing a different pronunciation.

sourceWitness.citation: Shangshu, Jun Shi; traditional commentary in Shangshu Yaoyi 16
sourceWitness.excerpt: 祖乙時有巫賢...巫賢咸之子

decisions.after: In Zu Yi's time, there was another Wu Xian, son of the preceding Wu Xian;
decisions.reason: The literal field retains standard pinyin and states the traditionally attested relationship that distinguishes 巫賢 from the preceding 巫咸; Wade-Giles for only one of the two would be inconsistent.

decisions.after: The ruler of Yan escorted Duke Huan across the border into Qi. Duke Huan then ceded to Yan all the Qi territory through which the ruler of Yan had accompanied him and required Yan to resume paying tribute to the Son of Heaven, as it had in the time of Chengzhou;
decisions.reason: The Yan ruler had escorted Duke Huan beyond Yan's border into Qi land. 燕所至地 is the Qi territory reached by that escort, not territory conquered by Duke Huan; 共貢 here is the obligation to furnish tribute, not a joint payment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 燕君送齊桓公出境，桓公因割燕所至地予燕，使燕共貢天子

decisions.after: General Shi Bei and the common people counterattacked Crown Prince Ping. Shi Bei was killed, and his body was displayed as a warning.
decisions.reason: The repeated subject 將軍市被 identifies Shi Bei, not Ping, as the man who died and whose body was displayed. Naming him again removes the English pronoun ambiguity.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 將軍市被及百姓反攻太子平，將軍市被死，以徇

decisions.after: King Yi reigned for twelve years and died. His son Kuai of Yan succeeded him.
decisions.reason: 立十二年 states the length of King Yi's reign. The revision also renders 燕噲 as the natural English 'Kuai of Yan' and supplies the understood object of 'succeeded.'

sourceWitness.excerpt: 易王立十二年卒，子燕噲立

decisions.after: Guo Kui said: "If Your Majesty truly wishes to attract scholars, begin with me.
decisions.reason: 必欲 expresses genuine determination, not an obligation to wish. The direct address 王 is clearer as 'Your Majesty,' matching the surrounding audience.

decisions.after: Yan saw that Zhao had repeatedly been hard-pressed by Qin, that Lian Po had left, and that Pang Nuan had been appointed general. Hoping to take advantage of Zhao's exhaustion, Yan decided to attack.
decisions.reason: Pang Nuan was Zhao's general, as the following sentence confirms. Yan observes Zhao's circumstances and then decides to attack; it does not appoint Pang Nuan.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 令龐煖將也...趙使龐煖擊之

decisions.after: Yan saw that Zhao had repeatedly been hard pressed by Qin, that Lian Po had departed, and that Pang Nuan had been appointed general, and wanted to take advantage of Zhao's exhaustion to attack it.
decisions.reason: The literal field must also keep Pang Nuan's appointment inside the description of Zhao rather than assigning that action to Yan.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 燕見趙數困于秦，而廉頗去，令龐煖將也...趙使龐煖擊之
